agent: the collecting session of the diplomatic state wave - the diplomacy screen's triangle, faction boxes and leftover tooltips
question: What the diplomacy screen's triangle markers, faction boxes and the tooltips briefs D and E left unread put on screen, for OpenHOI3's building of the screen: the markers' placement, the boxes, the drift tooltip's order and rounding, a faction's rules and modifier text, the victory share's tooltip, the relation's breakdown and the war ceiling's tooltip.

addresses.name: CRule::DescribeSetRules
addresses.comment: CRule slot 7 (vftable 0x15BC708), 0x45DE60 to the `ret 4` at 0x45E1C4. **Every rule that is set, one a line**: for i in 0..3 (the four rule definitions of the global vector at 0x1A862C0, made by InitRuleDefinitions), where the rule's bool (this +0x18 + i*8) is set: a newline where the text grew since the last line written, the definition's localised name (CModifierDefinition_GetLocalisedName on its key, +4), ": ", a colour - §G where the definition's flag (+0x28) is set, else §R; all four definitions have it set - the localised `YES`, and §W. A rule that is not set writes nothing, so a faction with none writes an empty string. Its one reader on the diplomacy screen is CFaction_DescribeRulesAndModifier (0x122AF0). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.5.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled and read end to end: the loop runs local_18 from 0 in steps of 4 to 0xF and local_14 from this+0x18 in steps of 8; the colour strings are 0x15B5C50 '§G' and 0x15B5C58 '§R' by image.read; the flag is the `push 1` at 0x45D4EF and its siblings in InitRuleDefinitions. Wrong if a set rule did not appear in the axis faction's tooltip in a running game.

addresses.name: CRule::DescribeRule
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __thiscall CRule::DescribeRule(CRule* this, Hoi3CString* out, int rule)
addresses.comment: CRule slot 8, 0x45DB60 to the `ret 8` at 0x45DE3B. One rule's line whether it is set or not: the object's own slot 6 - in CRule's table GetEmptyName (0x456DD0), so nothing, where DescribeSetRules names the definition - then ": ", a colour (§G set, §R not, where the definition's flag +0x28 is set; the other way round where it is not), the localised `YES` or `NO`, §W. Not called from the diplomacy screen. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.5.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the branch on `this[rule*2+6]` and on the definition's +0x28 picks between 0x15B5C50 and 0x15B5C58, then YES or NO. The callers were not read, so its use is unknown; wrong if the second argument were not a rule index.

addresses.name: InitRuleDefinitions
addresses.comment: Builds the four rule definitions into the global vector at 0x1A862C0, once (it returns at once when the vector is not empty), in this order, each a 0x2C-byte CRuleDefinition: 0 `NONE` (save token 0x18D), 1 `RULE_LIMITED_WAR` (0x4BD), 2 `RULE_ALLIANCE_GUARANTEE` (0x4BE), 3 `RULE_FREE_RESOURCE_GIFTS` (0x4BF), every one with the flag +0x28 set (`push 1`). The tokens are the file keys `limited_war`, `allience_wide_guarantee` (so spelled) and `free_resource_gifts`, which CRule::LoadKey matches against a definition's +0x20. 0x45D4A0 to the bare `ret` at 0x45D65A. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.5.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the four strings are pushed at 0x45D501 ('NONE') and from 0x15BC684/0x15BC698/0x15BC6B0; the token immediates 0x18D, 0x4BD, 0x4BE, 0x4BF; the three file keys sit together at 0x15E7A5C..0x15E7A88. Wrong if the token-to-key mapping were other than the names' order in the save-token table.

addresses.name: CRuleDefinition::CRuleDefinition
addresses.signature: CRuleDefinition* __stdcall CRuleDefinition::CRuleDefinition(CRuleDefinition* this, SaveToken token, Hoi3CString key, bool flag, int index@EDX) @EAX
addresses.comment: 0x45D410 to the `ret 0x28` at 0x45D487. vftable 0x15BC6F4; the key string at +4, the save token at +0x20, the index (EDX) at +0x24, the flag byte at +0x28 (the one CRule's text colours by). Four callers, all in InitRuleDefinitions. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.5.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled end to end: `mov [esi+0x24], edx`, `mov [esi+0x20], [ebp+0xc]`, the string copied from [ebp+0x10], `mov cl, [ebp+0x2c]; mov [esi+0x28], cl`; ret 0x28 = this + token + a 0x1C string + the flag.

addresses.name: CCountry_BuildRelationChangeBreakdown
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CCountry_BuildRelationChangeBreakdown(CCountry* country, Hoi3CString* out, CCountryTag other)
addresses.comment: **The delayed half of a relation row's tooltip on the diplomacy screen.** 0x4E74D0, `ret 0x10` at 0x4E75D3 and 0x4E78C5. With T = country->+0xE28[other.id]: where T's relation (+0x38) is above 100000 and MonthlyRelationDrift(country, other) is not negative, the localised `RELATION_CAPPED` alone. Otherwise one line each, in this order, through FormatRelationChangeLine: DIPRELCH_DEPENDENCY where T +0x18 is set, DIPRELCH_WAR where T +0x20 is set, DIPRELCH_NBOR_PEACE where other is on country's neighbour flags (+0xF58), other is not at war and country is not (+0xACC), DIPRELCH_GUARANTEE where T +0x1C is set, DIPRELCH_HASACCESS where T +0x4C is set. Each figure is a float constant floored - 250.5, -99.5, 50.5, 80.5, 25.5 at 0x160A688, 0x160A750, 0x160A7B4, 0x160A6D8, 0x160A828 - so 250, -100, 50, 80 and 25, the month's drift of each term, and not the pair's own drift. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.7.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the five floats read as floats with image.read; the order is the order of the branches in the body. Its caller is CRelationEntry::BuildTooltip's delayed half (E.4 named 0x4E74D0). Wrong if the floats were defines patched at load - nothing writes those addresses in the image's reference list.

addresses.name: FormatRelationChangeLine
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall FormatRelationChangeLine(Hoi3CString* out, int drift, Hoi3CString key)
addresses.comment: One line of the relation's breakdown: "§G+" where drift > 0, "§Y" at 0, "§R" below (0x15B6B84, 0x15B5C54, 0x15B5C58), then FormatFloat of drift in single precision / 1000.0 x 12.0 to two places ('%.2f', rounded) - a month's figure made a year's - then "§W: ", the key's text and "\n". 0x4E72A0 to the `ret 0x24` at 0x4E74CD; the key is a std::string by value. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.7.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled 0x4E7304..0x4E7337: cvtdq2ps, divsd by the double 1000.0 at 0x160A300, mulsd by 12.0 at 0x160AA48, then call 0xA5AEC0 with 2; the three prefixes read with image.read; 0x15C1050 is '§W: '.

addresses.name: CFaction_DescribeRulesAndModifier
addresses.comment: **The delayed half of a faction button's tooltip.** The faction's rule (+0x40, a CRule) by its slot 7, CRule::DescribeSetRules, then "\n", then its modifier (+0x7C, a CModifier subclass with vftable 0x15C2454) by its slot 7, CModifier::DescribeAllValues. The faction arrives in EDI; 0x522AF0 to the `ret 4` at 0x522BB3. Two callers in CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip: `faction_symbol_big_button` and `faction_symbol_button`, the second adding the victory conditions' "\n%d/%d". See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.3 and F.5.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled: `(**(code **)(*(int *)(unaff_EDI + 0x40) + 0x1c))` and the same on +0x7C; the CFaction constructor makes +0x40 with 0x45D7B0 (vftable 0x15BC708, CRule) and +0x7C with vftable 0x15C2454, whose slot 7 is 0x459AB0, DescribeAllValues.

addresses.name: CFaction_BuildProgressTooltip
addresses.comment: `victory_progress`'s tooltip on the diplomacy screen's faction box: FACTION_PROGRESS_DESC with TOTAL = the sum of every map province's victory points x 1000, share = Progress (+0xAC) x 1000 / TOTAL where TOTAL is not 0 (else Progress), PERCENT = FormatFixedPoint(share x 100000 / 1000, 2), OUR = FormatFixedPoint(Progress, 0), TOTAL = FormatFixedPoint(TOTAL, 0), WHO = the faction's slot 6. 0x522E00 to the `ret 8` at 0x5233F3. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.6.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the loop over provinces_begin..end adds g_CMap->provinces[i]->victory_points * 1000; param_1[0x2B] is +0xAC. One caller, CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip at the `victory_progress` branch.

addresses.name: CFaction::GetLocalisedName
addresses.comment: CFaction slot 6 (vftable 0x15C2430): GetText of the faction's tag string (+0xC), rendered with the game's colours - so `axis` gives "Axis". 0x522590 to the `ret 4` at 0x522633. What every diplomacy-screen text calls the faction's 'slot 6 text'. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.2.
addresses.evidence: Disassembled: `add ecx, 0xc; push ecx; ... call 0xA82490` (GetText) then 0x45FF30 (GetGameSettings) and 0xA82E40 (Render) with the settings' colours at +0x6C/+0x74. The only table holding it is CFaction's, slot 6.

addresses.name: VictoryConditions_CountForFaction

Bare `ret`s at 0x543D90 and 0x543DA7. One of the two counts behind the faction button's "\n%d/%d"; that the object is the game state's victory conditions and what each element is were not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.10.

addresses.comment: A node of the drift tooltip's sorted list: a GuiTooltipText copied from this (0x5C), the faction name string at +0x5C, the total at +0x78, prev at +0x7C, next at +0x80, a byte at +0x84 cleared. 0x50F060 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x50F0DA. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.4.

addresses.name: DriftTooltipEntry::InsertSorted
addresses.comment: Puts a drift tooltip entry into its list, highest total first: walks from the tail (list +4) back through +0x7C to the first node whose total (+0x78) is at least the entry's, and puts the new node after it (at the tail where that is the tail); where none is, 0x512DD0 puts it at the head. So of equal totals the one added earlier stays in front. 0x5108E0, four `ret 4`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.4.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; `if (this+0x78 <= node+0x78)` then insert after node, else `node = node+0x7C`; the fall-through calls 0x512DD0 (not read; a push to the front by its place in the logic).

addresses.name: CCountry_BuildMaxNeutralityForWarTooltip
addresses.signature: Hoi3CString* __stdcall CCountry_BuildMaxNeutralityForWarTooltip(CCountry* country, Hoi3CString* out, CCountryTag* other)
addresses.comment: The text twin of CCountry::GetMaxNeutralityForWarWith, and `label_our_neutrality_value`'s tooltip. Lines appended in order: WARNE_THREAT with VAL = FormatFixedPoint(the larger of country's threat from other and other's from country, 0), not floored; WARNE_CLAIMS with VAL = FormatFixedPoint(NEUT_REDUCTION_AT_CLAIMS, 0) where the `aquire_all_cores` casus belli is valid, usable for the pair and 0x47BC60 answers true after 0x4797C0; WARNE_CONTINENT with VAL = FormatFixedPoint(NEUT_INCREASE_DIFF_CONTINENT, 0) where the two capitals' continents differ and other is not on country's neighbour flags (+0xF58); WARNE_FACTION where country's faction's neutrality (CFaction +0xB0) is not 0, NAME the faction's slot 6 and VAL '§G+' (or '§R' where negative) + FormatFixedPoint(neutrality, 0). 0x505F20 to the `ret 0xC` at 0x5067CB. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md, F.8.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled; the four keys in that order; the defines are diplomacy[0x37] and [0x36], which GetMaxNeutralityForWarWith's record places at +0xDC and +0xD8. Wrong if `other` were passed by value - `mov ecx, [ebp+0x10]; mov eax, [ecx+4]` reads through it.

0x47BC60 and 0x4797C0 - the claims test inside the war ceiling and its tooltip
0x543D70/0x543DB0's object - the game state's victory conditions, what an element is and what +0x68 means
